analysis.title: NY Open - Heading to the polls
key_insights: US midterms are today. 435 House seats, 35 of 100 Senate seats and 36 governor races are up. Prediction markets see a high probability of a Democratic sweep, but margins will drive Wednesday's market moves.

Senate outcome matters most. Swing-state results are likely from about 22:00 ET based on historical call times. Texas is the key bellwether (polls close 20:00 ET), and a Democratic win there could signal a broader blue wave.

Republicans hold the House 219-213 (three vacancies) and the Senate 53-47, including two independents who caucus with Democrats. Cook Political Report sees Democrats winning 227-240 House seats, with 218 needed for a majority. Of the 35 Senate seats up, Republicans hold 22 and Democrats 13, and 11 states are competitive.

A Democratic sweep is increasingly priced in. Citi equity strategists see incremental pressure on equities only if Democrats win more than 53 Senate seats. Citi's quant team finds credit, rates and equities all underperform in election years, but a post-election relief rally unwinds this by year-end.

FX spot reaction to the election is expected to be minimal (EURUSD at 35bp implied) but reflects risks beyond the election, such as geopolitical escalation. The Q4 refunding announcement on Wednesday is arguably more in focus for USTs.

RBA hiked 25bp with a 6-3 vote split. The statement dropped the reference to hiking further if needed, and Governor Bullock said there is time to take stock. OIS curves repriced and AUD weakened. Citi's economists see no further hikes but risks skewed to higher rates in 2027.

Citi strategists say a December RBA hike is off the table barring a shock October CPI, but February is live if trimmed-mean inflation is in line with 0.9%. They see value in paying February and receiving further out, which makes front-end flatteners appealing.

PBoC raised the FX reserve requirement ratio by 2 points to 6%, draining an estimated $20bn of dollar supply. USDCNH spiked above 6.67. The move appears aimed at narrowing the spot-fixing spread from about 700 pips to around -250 to -300 pips. Citi's desk expects consolidation and resistance near 6.6750-6.6800, and says the RMB appreciation trend remains intact but is now firmly managed.

Oil fell nearly 8% Monday and Brent is up 1.57% at print. The US conducted targeted strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz area, including Qeshm Island, per WSJ. Reuters reports the US and Iran are far from a deal to end the war. Gold is down 0.9%, and Citi flags $3900 as support to watch.
Large-cap equity positioning has eased amid AI jitters, and Nasdaq is now flat. Citi's Equity Markets Positioning Model shows S&P 500 and Nasdaq positioning closer to neutral. Kospi closed -3.5%.

Apple beat on earnings after Monday's close, but the December outlook was mixed: higher product revenue was partly offset by lower services growth and gross margins. Citi remains constructive on the long-term trajectory.

Citi's trader recently went long EURUSD (bearish USD), expecting USD to stay under pressure from AI strains. Long USD positioning was reduced last week but is still elevated at +5.8, mostly by real money and retail. Hedge funds have already shifted bearish USD. The London trader keeps an AUDNZD short.

market_movers.rationale: Citi remains constructive on Apple's long-term trajectory after an earnings beat with a mixed December outlook: higher product revenue offset by lower services growth and gross margins.

sector_views.rationale: Citi's CETS team hopes for post-midterm relief in the sector (CGUSPGEN) but says uncertainty is too high to pursue it yet.

earnings_insights: Apple reported after the close Monday and beat on earnings. The December outlook was mixed: higher product revenues were partially offset by lower services growth and gross margins. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Vote split and Bullock's wait-and-see tone were read as dovish. AU bonds outperformed and AUD weakened.

macro_indicators.reading: 0.9% (level for a February hike to stay live)
macro_indicators.interpretation: If trimmed mean comes in line with 0.9%, Citi sees February as live for another RBA hike.
Stronger than expected, with MoM about 0.2%. The next SNB meeting is in December, and the SNB is expected to hold indefinitely for now.
Supported by AI-related merchandise trade and rising investment. QoQ growth was 1.9% after -0.6% prior.
Persistent inflation pressure. Citi economists look to the November 12 inflation report for guidance.
Drains an estimated $20bn of dollar supply and targets the spot-fixing spread.

trade_ideas.rationale: USD is expected to remain under pressure from AI strains, and positioning risks are skewed toward USD selling ahead of events.
The RBNZ's decision not to hike was less dovish than the headline reaction, the Nov 7 election may not be as negative as expected, and seasonal patterns are bearish.

trade_ideas.risk: A shock October CPI or trimmed mean above 0.9% could keep a February hike live.

tension_points.bear_case: Citi's equity strategists see incremental pressure if Democrats win more than 53 Senate seats, and strategists see higher escalation risks under a divided Congress.
